docs.title: StarPilot FAQ and Troubleshooting
docs.text: Can't find an answer to your question? Post in Discord or submit feedback through the ticket system.

docs.title: How do I submit feedback?
docs.text:
Important

StarPilot thrives on the feedback and responsiveness of our community. If you are experiencing an issue, please open a ticket and share what you are seeing. The more people submitting feedback, the better your car (and everyone else's) can drive.

Use the StarPilot ticket system to report bugs, share tuning feedback, request features, or ask for an issue to be investigated. The guide explains which button to choose and what information to include.

docs.title: What is StarPilot?
docs.text: StarPilot is a standalone, community-driven fork of openpilot. It runs on comma 3, 3X, and 4 and adds driving, device management, and customization features. See the StarPilot overview and installation guide.

docs.title: What is the Galaxy? Can I change settings from my phone?
docs.text: Galaxy is StarPilot's browser interface for settings, routes, and device tools. Local access works without Internet. Remote access uses a password protected galaxy.firestar.link link and needs Internet. See Access Galaxy.

docs.title: Does StarPilot support Comma 3, 3X, and 4?
docs.text: Yes. StarPilot fully supports all three comma devices, including features that stock openpilot has dropped on older hardware (such as the Comma 3). See the Comma Devices page for details.

docs.title: Does StarPilot support Chestnut (external GPU)?
docs.text: Yes. StarPilot detects Chestnut on Comma 3, 3X, and 4 and unlocks chestnut-class driving models when the hardware is ready. Most users do not need Chestnut - see the Chestnut page.

docs.title: Why is my car driving terribly?
docs.text: It may be a bad setting. Try enabling safe mode to revert to all defaults. If that fixes it, reset your toggles to defaults. If not, create a troubleshooting thread in the discord.

docs.title: Will installing openpilot void my warranty?
docs.text: https://comma.ai/support#will-installing-a-comma-device-void-my-warranty

docs.title: Is the openpilot install reversible?
docs.text:
Yes. The openpilot hardware install is fully reversible. There are no car modifications, just custom harnesses that intercept at the existing harnesses.

When the comma USB-C is unplugged, your car can't tell the difference.

When the openpilot hardware (camera harnesses, pedal, ASCM, SASCM, SDSU, SDGM, etc.) are removed, the car returns to stock.

docs.title: Will openpilot navigate on its own?
docs.text: No. Navigation & Maps displays a route and helps the driving model prepare for turns. You still steer through intersections and exits and remain responsible for the drive.

docs.title: How do I clear the "LKAS Fault: Restart the car" error?
docs.text:
1. Turn your car off
  2. Open your car door
  3. Wait 2 minutes (you can close your door in the meantime)
  4. Turn car on
  5. Done. LKAS fault should have cleared.

docs.title: How do I avoid LKAS faults?
docs.text: 1. Never reboot, unplug, or power off the comma while your car is on. This will cause an LKAS fault.

docs.title: How do I clear the "Cruise Fault: Restart the car" error?
docs.text:
This error applies only to vehicles with adaptive cruise control (ACC).

  1. Turn car off
  2. Open car door
  3. Close car door
  4. Turn car on
  5. Wait 5 seconds
  6. If your error is cleared, you are done. If the error is still present, go back to step 1. This can take 6 or more tries.

docs.title: How do I clear the "Controls Mismatch" error?
docs.text:
1. Turn car off
  2. Wait 5 seconds
  3. Turn car on

If the error persists, restart the comma device with the car off.

Note

Remote Start Issues If you use remote start and the "boot comma with remote start" setting is enabled, to avoid issues, you should cycle the car off and then back on again after you get in. Otherwise, you might get the Controls Mismatch error.

docs.title: How do I upload logs for troubleshooting?
docs.text:
Logs are sent as routes. A route is a single drive (from car on to car off), with 1 minute segments. Log data contains all Openpilot data: video, comms, gps, etc.

  1. Navigate to connect.comma.ai
  2. Find the route your issue happened on and click on it.
  3. Click and drag the video slider over the section where the error happened. The video will loop over this selected section, make sure the error is within. To undo your last selection, click the back arrow just above the video slider. Once you are happy with the segments selected, proceed to the next step.
  4. Click Files, then next to All logs, click (upload ## logs)
  5. Wait for data to be uploaded (you can check the progress using Files > View Upload Queue)
  6. Click More info, then enable Public access and copy the Route info using the Copy button:
  7. Create a ticket using the buttons in the #submit-feedback-and-reports channel of the Discord server. Be as descriptive as possible. Also include the approximate minute(s) in the route it happened. StarPilot has a unique, community-focused ticketing system that helps users and developers make sure no problem goes unresolved. Learn how it works and what to include in your report.

Tip

Ending a route log early To make it easier to find the error, you can force the log to end early using: Settings > Utilities > Force offroad. This will make sure the error is near the end of the log.

docs.title: I'm stuck on the boot logo screen. How do I fix it?
docs.text:
This is usually caused by a sticky param, especially when coming from another openpilot fork.

  1. Unplug the device
  2. Wait 60 seconds
  3. Plug it back in
  4. Tap the center of the screen over and over until the reset prompt comes up
  5. Reset
  6. Install using link: starpilothq/saveme
  7. After the device boots, use the branch switcher to go back to StarPilot

If issues persist, reach out in Discord.

Important

If Galaxy still works, open Logs & Diagnostics → Troubleshoot → Show Non-Default Values and review changed settings before using a recovery branch.

docs.title: My device is behaving oddly. What is a "saveme"?
docs.text:
Sometimes the device can get into a bad state due to a bad setting or conflicts during updates (especially if you went a long time without updating). A "saveme" will reset all settings and return to near new state (without require a flash).

If Galaxy still works, open Logs & Diagnostics → Troubleshoot → Show Non-Default Values. Use Reset Selected or Reset All Non-Default Settings and confirm. This resets available saved settings, not the entire device.

docs.title: How do I fix the "CAN bus disconnected" Error?
docs.text: Openpilot had an issue communicating on the CAN bus. Reseat (unplug and plug back in) all of your openpilot connections (harnesses, OBD-C, pedal, etc).

docs.title: Ticket System
docs.text: StarPilot thrives on the feedback and responsiveness of our community. If you are experiencing an issue, please open a ticket and share what you are seeing. The more people submitting feedback, the better your car (and everyone else's) can drive.

docs.title: What is it?
docs.text: The Discord ticket system is the main way to report problems and request support for StarPilot. Create a ticket if your car meets Comma's requirements but is not yet supported by StarPilot, if you experience ping-ponging or steering wobble, or if you encounter another issue that requires investigation. For basic configuration questions, ask in the appropriate public support channel instead. Firestar will review your ticket when available and may release an update to address the issue.

docs.title: Before creating a ticket!
docs.text:
You must first be a member of the StarPilot Discord server.

Potential fixes are first released on the Dom branch. If you are using the Starpilot branch, you will need to switch to Dom to test the update.

docs.title: How do I create a ticket?
docs.text:
1. Open the StarPilot Discord.
  2. Go to the #submit-feedback-and-reports channel.

  3. Select the appropriate report button.

  4. Get your route information and upload your logs. Add that information to the form, describe the problem or requested feature in as much detail as possible, and select Submit.

docs.title: Which button should I choose?
docs.text:
Bug Report Use Bug Report when something is not working correctly. For example, use it if a steering-wheel button no longer works as expected. Feedback Use Feedback for non-urgent tuning concerns, such as insufficient steering performance or steering wobble. Feature Request Use Feature Request to suggest a new StarPilot feature. If you request a feature, be prepared to test it. View My Reports Use View My Reports to see a list of your reports and their current status.

Tip

If you can reproduce the issue, open a bookmark on your device shortly before it occurs and close the bookmark shortly afterward. Include the bookmark information in your ticket to help Firestar locate and investigate the issue.

docs.title: How do I switch from the Starpilot branch to Dom?
docs.text:
Switch to the Dom branch while parked using the software guide. You do not need to reinstall StarPilot.

Tip

If you do not want to remain on Dom, wait until the fix is included in the next StarPilot release. You can then follow the same process to switch back to the Starpilot branch.

docs.title: What do the colored circles on my ticket mean?
docs.text:
Each colored circle represents the current status of your ticket.

Color Meaning What you should do 🟠 Your ticket is new and has been submitted. Wait for Firestar to review it. ⚪ Firestar has reviewed your ticket, but an update is not ready yet. The circle will turn purple when the update is ready to test. Please be patient and wait for the circle to turn purple. 🟣 Your ticket has been reviewed and a potential fix is ready. Update Dom and test the fix. If the problem remains, submit a new route and updated logs. 🔴 Your ticket was sent back for further investigation. Wait for the ticket to return to purple status. 🟢 You closed the ticket yourself. No further action is required. 🔵 A staff member or the bot closed your ticket. No further action is required.

docs.title: Vehicle Quirks
docs.text:
Things to be aware of for your vehicle relating to openpilot:

  • Openpilot cannot steer below 7 mph.
  • Non-ACC Bolts are limited to regen-only braking using a Comma Pedal. This means a max 70kW of deceleration meaning no emergency stops and poor low-speed slowing performance. You will occasionally need to brake manually.
  • ACC Bolts without a pedal are limited to 10kW of regen (but unlike non-ACC, openpilot can control your friction brakes).
    • With a Comma Pedal, openpilot blends friction braking with up to 70kW of regen. See ACC Bolts.
  • ACC Bolts without a pedal do not have stop and go support (press accelerator pedal or press CC resume).
    • ACC and non-ACC Bolts with a Comma Pedal do have stop-and-go support.
  • 22-23 Bolts only: Sport mode will decrease available steering torque.
  • NNFF should not be used with Bolts.
  • The regen paddle can be used to disengage openpilot.
  • Steering wheel LKAS button and light do not work when comma is connected (purely a cosmetic issue).
    • If pressed, the dash will display "LKAS is unavailable" but op steering will still work.
    • The button also cannot be used with the openpilot custom button actions (ACC models can still use the distance button).

docs.title: StarPilot Settings
docs.text: Enable Disable Automatic Fingerprint Detection and manually select your vehicle make and model. Fingerprinting can be inconsistent on GM vehicles, and an ACC Bolt can sometimes be detected as a non-ACC Bolt, leaving it without gas or brake control.

docs.title: Tires
docs.text:
• Keep your tires at the recommended 38 psi.
  • Keep your car aligned.
  • Swapping tires is okay, but don't change wheel sizes. Changing wheel sizes can cause issues.

docs.title: One Pedal Driving/L Mode
docs.text: StarPilot with the Comma Pedal relies on one pedal driving to slow down. You must have your car in One Pedal mode on Gen 2 Bolts or L mode on Gen 0 and Gen 1 Bolts.

docs.title: Sport Mode
docs.text: It is generally recommended to leave Sport Mode off. The Map Accel/Decel to Gears setting allows you to use the Sport Mode button to change between acceleration profiles, but Sport Mode changes the lateral response on Gen 2 cars and gives you less steering torque.

docs.text:
1. Comma 4
  2. GM Harness and Harness Box
  3. Comma Pedal (optional, but strongly recommended for non-ACC cars)

Tip

We recommend purchasing from BearTechWorkshop (aka tinybear) whenever possible. They are a small business providing the openpilot community with high quality products and excellent customer support.

Comma Power is not needed

The Comma Power cable is not needed for most GM vehicles (eg. bolt and volt).

docs.title: Should I buy a Comma Pedal?
docs.text: Our recommendation for whether or not to purchase the pedal depends on if your car is ACC or Non-ACC.

docs.title: Non-ACC Bolts
docs.text:
In non-ACC bolts, the Comma Pedal is strongly recommended. It allows openpilot to accelerate and decelerate using regen braking and one pedal driving mode (the L gear). It is also capable of stop-and-go (the main reason for comma pedal on other vehicles).

The only reasons to not use a pedal interceptor with your non-ACC Bolt are cost or if you are uncomfortable with the idea of installing the pedal interceptor.

Without the pedal, openpilot is very limited in its ability to control the speed of your vehicle. It will operate using a workaround we call "CCLong" or "Redneck ACC".

docs.title: ACC Bolts
docs.text:
In ACC bolts, openpilot can request gas and brake commands through ACC commands. Without a pedal, brake commands only use the friction brakes to slow down and regen braking is limited to 10kW (same as coasting in D mode), and it cannot stop-and-go.

Adding a comma pedal is now the best of both worlds. StarPilot blends your friction brakes with regen, so an ACC Bolt with a pedal gets both full friction braking and up to 70 kW of regen, plus stop-and-go support. This removes the old tradeoff where adding a pedal meant giving up openpilot's access to the friction brakes.

For ACC Bolts, a pedal is optional but recommended if you want stronger regen-based slowing and stop-and-go, with no downside to your friction braking.

docs.title: Pedal Firmware Flashing
docs.text:
Gen 1 Bolts only (2017-2021)

Warning

If you purchased your pedal before June 2025 and have not updated the firmware, you will encounter issues with the current version of StarPilot.

The Gen 1 Bolt firmware released in October 2024 ran at twice the speed it should have. This was corrected in June 2025. Firmware from before October 2024 will run okay, but the newer firmware is better, so it is best to update.

docs.text:

USB cable requirement

USB-C to USB-C does not work for DFU flashing. There must be a USB-A port somewhere in the chain, such as USB-A to USB-C or USB-A to micro-USB. The DFU key/pedal is a USB 2.0 device and does not include USB-C circuitry, so a C-to-C cable often will not provide VBUS or enumerate the device.

docs.title: Propulsion Power Reduced and Regen Not Working
docs.text:
Your Bolt may have had a momentary issue communicating with the throttle pedal, causing it to enter a limp mode.

  1. Turn off the car.
  2. Unplug all connectors for the Comma Pedal.
  3. Breathe hot "sultry" air into the connector ends. This includes the two connectors coming out of the Comma Pedal box and the car side, if possible. This is hot breath like fogging up a window, not blowing out a candle.
  4. Reconnect all connectors.

If the issue still persists, post in the troubleshooting thread.

docs.title: How to Set Up Long on Some HDA2 Vehicles
docs.text:
This is how to set up long on:

  • Ioniq 6 HDA2 2023-2025
  • EV9 HDA2 2024-2026
  • Ioniq 5 2026 HDA2

docs.title: First-Time Things to Toggle
docs.text:
1. Toggle on Disable Automatic Fingerprint Detection in Settings > StarPilot > Vehicle Settings.
  2. Set Car Make to Hyundai.
  3. Set Car Model to your car model. In my instance, this is Hyundai Ioniq 6 (with HDA II) 2023-2024.
  4. Toggle on openpilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha) in Settings > Developer.

docs.title: Every-Time Startup Procedure
docs.text:
1. Make sure the car is off.
  2. Keep your foot off the brake.
  3. Press the start button twice.
  4. Wait for the comma to fully turn on to an onroad state.
  5. Wait for the cruise-control indicator on the dash to show --- MPH or HDA 25.
  6. Push the brake pedal down.
  7. Hit the start button once.

Long should be enabled now!

docs.title: Engaging Long After You See --- MPH/KPH
docs.text:
Our wheel controls are slightly different from other forks:

  • LKAS button = Always on Lateral (M.A.D.S.)
  • Cruise button = Always on Lateral (M.A.D.S.)
  • Cruise knob down = Activate long at the current speed
  • Cruise knob in = Deactivate long
  • Cruise knob up = Turn long back on at the previously set speed

After it's engaged:

  • Cruise knob down = Lower the max-speed threshold
  • Cruise knob up = Raise the max-speed threshold

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If the openpilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha) toggle is grayed out, try one of these:

  1. Restart the comma.
  2. Turn off the car, turn off the comma, and wait for the comma to shut off completely. Then go through the every-time startup procedure again.

docs.title: Brand-wide tuning improvements
docs.text:
These improvements apply to every car of the brand, including models already supported by stock:

  • All Hyundai / Kia / Genesis — higher max acceleration
  • All Honda / Acura — smoother stops
  • All Toyota (TSS2 torque cars) — lateral tuning refinement
  • All GM — smoother low-speed braking and reworked gas/regen response

Tuned identically to stock

Mazda, Tesla (Model 3 / Y), Nissan, and Volkswagen existing platforms use the same tuning as stock openpilot (StarPilot only changes their features/toggles, not tuning).

docs.title: Required Hardware - Volt & Other ASCM/SDGM Cars
docs.text:
The Volt has a number of possible configurations. This page lists the recommended method per car type, and all possible methods.

There are two parts to OpenPilot control: Lateral Control (Steering) & Longitudinal Control (Gas/Brake).

ASCM & SDGM give the comma control over steering. Your car's ACC will function as normal.

SASCM allows you to override the built in ACC and use OpenPilot Longitudinal control. If you have stock ACC and do not wish to use OpenPilot Long, you can just purchase the ASCM/SDGM portion of the suggestions.

docs.title: Recommended Config per Car Model
docs.text:
• 2017-2018 Chevy Volt with Factory ACC: ASCM Harness & SASCM
  • 2019 Chevy Volt with Factory ACC: SDGM Harness & SASCM
  • Volts without Factory ACC: Volts without ACC
  • Non-Volt Car with ASCM: ASCM Harness & SASCM
  • Non-Volt Car with SDGM: SDGM Harness & SASCM

Tip

We recommend purchasing from BearTechWorkshop (aka tinybear) whenever possible. They are a small business providing the openpilot community with high quality products and excellent customer support.

Comma Power is not needed

The Comma Power cable is not needed for most GM vehicles (eg. bolt and volt).

The 12V power is provided by the camera harness (or OBD for non-LKAS vehicles) and remains on while the car is powered off.

docs.title: Flashing Volt Firmware
docs.text:
Caution

Flashing your car's firmware is at your own risk. Unlike the custom harness installs, flashing is not reversible by simply unplugging hardware.

pinballben is the resident expert on flashing Volt firmware, who will provide the instructions and hardware for a fee. DM on Discord (through the member list).

Flashing ACC

Flashing ACC will remove stock CC. This can be restored by re-flashing stock firmware.

docs.title: GM Vehicle Settings
docs.text: Enable Disable Automatic Fingerprint Detection and manually select your vehicle make and model. Fingerprinting can be inconsistent on GM vehicles, so it is best to select the car manually.

docs.title: What is Redneck ACC (aka CC Long)?
docs.text:
This feature emulates a very basic ACC system by using the built-in cruise control system and then spamming virtual presses of the + and - buttons to control speed.

Redneck ACC is able to handle small speed variations while following a lead on the highway. However, it is unable to change speed fast enough to handle slowing or stopped leads or operate below 24 mph due to GM limitations, so you will be experiencing a small fraction of what openpilot is capable of. It is also quite jerky.

Do not expect it to stop for cars or react quickly. As always, be ready to intervene.

docs.title: GM LKAS Faults
docs.text: GM cars are very sensitive to the exact timing of the steering messages. Heat can cause thermal expansion of the connectors, so if an LKAS fault happens while driving, reseat your openpilot connections, such as the GM harness, OBD-C, and pedal ethernet. While reseating connectors, you can breathe hot air into the connector like fogging up a window, not blowing out a candle. This can help clear dust and dissipate static buildup.

docs.title: Bluetooth
docs.text:
Open Galaxy → Tools → Bluetooth while parked. Turn on Bluetooth, then use Pair phone or scan and press Pair beside a device. Confirm its code on both devices. Connect, Disconnect, and Forget manage saved pairings.

Controller Buttons assigns USB or Bluetooth gamepad, keyboard, or macropad buttons to Quick Select and driving screen actions. Turn off the vehicle before editing. Test buttons (20s) checks the input. These buttons do not control steering or pedals.

For music from your phone or Spotify, use StarPort → Spotify and Phone Audio. Pair the phone here first if using phone audio.

Comma 3 and 3X Big UI also has a Bluetooth screen for managing connections. Examples of add-on controls include a round controller and a strap controller.

docs.title: Cameras & Monitoring
docs.text: In Galaxy, Cameras & Monitoring contains the blind spot camera preview (PiP), Sentry, V-ASM spot monitoring, and a camera snapshot tool. Configure them while parked. For road-camera speed sign detection, see Vision speed limits.

docs.title: Camera Snapshot
docs.text: On the main Cameras & Monitoring page, turn off the vehicle, choose Cabin, Wide road, or Road, then tap Take snapshot. Use Clear to remove the preview. These snapshots are temporary and are not saved as Sentry events.

docs.title: V-ASM: adjacent spot monitoring
docs.text:
V-ASM adds visual spot warnings alongside factory blind spot monitoring, where available. It does not confirm that a lane is clear or change vehicle controls. Always check mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

Why the window regions are required: The cabin camera also sees the driver, pillars, and interior. V-ASM uses each region to crop and mask the matching side-window view before checking it for a vehicle. This tells the model which side to inspect and keeps unrelated parts of the image out of its input. At least one side must be marked before monitoring can be enabled; mark both sides if you want warnings on both.

  1. In Galaxy, open Cameras & Monitoring → V-ASM while parked. Tap Take new snapshot to load the cabin camera image.
  2. Select Left or Right for the vehicle side you want to mark. The preview is mirrored, so the vehicle's left appears on the left; Galaxy stores it as camera right. The vehicle's right appears on the right and is stored as camera left.
  3. Tap around the visible side glass for that side, then repeat for the other side. Include the front and rear side windows and as much visible glass as practical. Leave out pillars, door frames, and interior; include a side mirror if visible through the glass. A B-pillar can be inside a continuous region if needed. Use Undo or Clear to fix points. Each region needs at least three points.
  4. Tap Save, review the region, and confirm. Then turn on Use visual spot monitoring under the saved settings. A drawn region by itself does not enable warnings.

Detection confidence sets how strong the model's evidence must be (0.80–1.00). Raising it may reduce false alerts but miss vehicles. Warning smoothing (0.01–0.50 seconds) controls how quickly warnings change; raising it reduces flicker but delays changes. Start with the defaults and adjust only if you notice a problem. Changes to these settings require the vehicle to be parked.

The cabin snapshot stays in your browser and is not uploaded by the region editor. If a warning is missing or incorrect, you can submit an edge case or read about the training data.

docs.title: PiP: blind spot camera preview
docs.text:
Blind Spot Camera and Preview shows a close-up of a cabin side window on the driving screen. It can appear when you signal, when the car reports a blind spot warning, or when V-ASM reports a visual spot warning. It is a view for the driver, not a second detection model.

In Galaxy, open Cameras & Monitoring → Blind Spot Camera and Preview while parked. Take a cabin snapshot, choose Left camera or Right camera, and place its circular crop over the matching side window. Adjust Crop size, then Save and confirm. Turn on Use blind spot camera and choose Show on turn signal, Show on blind spot warning, or both. The warning option responds to factory blind spot warnings and to V-ASM warnings when V-ASM is configured and enabled. You can position the onroad camera views with the layout editor.

PiP's circular crop controls what appears on screen. V-ASM's window regions control what its model analyzes; configure them separately. PiP also needs a live cabin camera and a crop for the side being shown.

docs.title: Sentry: parked motion events
docs.text: Open Cameras & Monitoring → Sentry for parked motion monitoring, saved events, and notifications. See the Sentry Mode guide for setup and event details.

docs.title: Lane Centering
docs.text:
Lane Centering is a StarPilot feature that helps keep your vehicle centered between detected lane lines while still allowing the End-to-End (E2E) model to control the driving path.

Instead of replacing the E2E model, Lane Centering works alongside it.

docs.title: How Does Lane Centering Work?
docs.text:
When both lane lines are detected clearly and confidently, StarPilot compares the E2E model's predicted path with the center of the lane.

If they differ, StarPilot applies a small, smooth correction toward the lane center while still allowing the E2E model to make driving decisions.

If the lane lines become unreliable, the lane width appears abnormal, you're changing lanes, or other required conditions aren't met, StarPilot automatically falls back to the normal E2E path.

docs.title: How Can I Tell Which Direction Lane Centering Is Correcting?
docs.text: When Lane Centering applies a correction, the lane line on the side it is pulling toward turns blue. This provides a visual indication of the direction Lane Centering is guiding the vehicle.

docs.title: How Do I Enable Lane Centering?
docs.text:
Lane Centering is enabled through StarPilot Galaxy.

  1. Open Galaxy in your browser.
  2. Open Toggles.
  3. Go to the Developer section.
  4. Find Lane Centering and enable it.

Tip

If you're having trouble finding the setting, in Galaxy's Toggle page, use the Search bar and search for Lane Centering.

Once enabled, you can also configure how Lane Centering behaves.

docs.title: What Is Lane Center Offset?
docs.text:
Lane Center Offset allows you to fine-tune where the vehicle sits within the lane.

For example, if you prefer the vehicle to drive slightly closer to the right side of the lane rather than directly in the center, you can adjust the offset to do so.

docs.title: What Is E2E Authority?
docs.text:
E2E Authority controls how much influence the E2E model has over Lane Centering.

Giving E2E more authority allows the model to deviate further from the center when it believes it should, such as when navigating around potholes or cyclists.

Increasing Lane Centering gives you a more traditional centered driving feel.

Important

Lane Centering does not prevent the E2E model from controlling the vehicle. It simply biases the predicted path toward the detected center of the lane when conditions allow.

docs.title: Navigation & Maps
docs.text: Galaxy sends a destination to your comma and shows route choices. Turn guidance works with every driving model. Steering and speed still follow your normal engagement settings.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text: While parked, open Galaxy → Tools → Navigation & Maps → Setup. Turn on Navigation and save a public Mapbox token (starts with pk.). GPS Source selects comma/car position or phone GPS. Phone sharing needs Bluetooth or local Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Plan a route
docs.text:
On Destination, search for a place or choose a saved or recent one. Tap a result to start guidance and choose an alternate route if offered. Change destination searches again. End navigation clears the route. The star saves a place as Home, Work, or another favorite.

Routes show traffic-aware choices and ETA when available. Galaxy reroutes after a route deviation. You can start or end guidance through the remote Galaxy link.

Offline Maps has two downloads: Map Overlay Roads keeps road lines on the car screen offline, while Speed Limit Maps saves regional speed-limit and curve data for the map provider. Downloading this data does not itself enable map-based SLC. Planning a new route still needs Internet.

Navigation assists with turns and exits. It does not complete them for you. Stay ready to steer. The route guidance builds on community work by Chubbs.

docs.title: Sentry Mode
docs.text:
When your car is parked, Sentry Mode watches for activity around your vehicle and automatically captures events, similar in spirit to Tesla's Sentry Mode, but built for your comma device and managed through Galaxy.

The best part: it is not running the cameras all day and draining your battery. Sentry stays dormant until something actually happens.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Sentry uses your comma device's accelerometer to detect movement while the vehicle is parked. The system sleeps quietly in the background and only wakes up when sustained motion is detected — for example, someone bumping your car or rocking it.

When that happens, Sentry captures camera images from the event and saves them for you to review later.

docs.title: Galaxy dashboard
docs.text:
Sentry is managed entirely through Galaxy. Open Cameras & Monitoring → Sentry to:

  • Turn Sentry Mode on or off
  • See the current status of the system
  • Review your latest event (with camera captures)
  • Browse past events and delete ones you no longer need
  • Grab a live snapshot from both cameras while parked
  • Send a test capture to confirm everything is working

Events refresh automatically while you have the page open, so you can check in from your phone without touching the comma device.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
When Sentry detects something, you can get alerted through any combination of:

  • Browser push notifications — enable directly from the Sentry page in Galaxy
  • ntfy — paste your ntfy topic URL for phone notifications
  • Discord — paste a Discord webhook URL (or any compatible webhook)

Use Send test notification in Galaxy to confirm your setup before you need it.

iPhone users

Add Galaxy to your Home Screen as a web app before enabling browser notifications. iOS requires a Home Screen web app for web push to work.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
All Sentry settings live on the Galaxy Sentry page — there is nothing extra to configure on the comma device itself.

Setting What it does Enable Sentry Mode Turn parked monitoring on or off Motion sensitivity How easily movement triggers Sentry. Lower values catch smaller bumps; higher values require stronger motion Warning persistence How long movement must continue before the first alert fires. Useful for filtering out brief vibrations (wind, passing trucks, etc.) Webhook URL Optional Discord or custom webhook for alerts ntfy URL Optional ntfy topic for phone alerts

Start with the defaults and adjust sensitivity if you get too many false alerts or not enough real ones.

docs.title: What gets captured
docs.text:
When Sentry triggers, it saves camera images from the event along with a timestamp. You can view them in Galaxy immediately or come back to them later from the event history.

Events stay on your device until you delete them.

Power-off alerts

If your comma device shuts down while Sentry is enabled, you may receive a power-off alert. These do not include camera images because the device is already shutting down.

Sentry is for when you are parked

Sentry only runs while your vehicle is off-road (not actively driving). It is a parking security feature, not something that runs during normal openpilot operation.

docs.title: Speed Limit Controller
docs.text:
The Speed Limit Controller, or SLC, limits StarPilot's maximum driving speed using the current posted speed limit plus a configurable offset. It can obtain speed limits from map data, the vehicle dashboard, and optional camera-based sign detection.

SLC does not replace the driver's judgment. Speed-limit information can be missing, delayed, or incorrect. Always follow posted signs and adjust the set speed when needed.

docs.title: Enable SLC
docs.text:
Open Toggles, then Longitudinal, and enable Speed Limit Controller. SLC and its related settings are available in the advanced settings tier.

When SLC is enabled, the driving screen shows the current speed limit below the maximum set speed. The optional offset display shows how far above or below the posted limit SLC is allowed to target.

docs.title: Driving-screen colors
docs.text:
The maximum set-speed color indicates what SLC is doing:

  • Red means SLC is actively limiting the maximum speed to the posted limit plus the configured offset.
  • Orange means the driver's maximum set speed is still active, but the vehicle is approaching the SLC limit.
  • The normal color means SLC is not currently limiting the maximum set speed.

docs.title: Speed-limit sources
docs.text:
SLC can use the following sources:

  • Dashboard reads a speed limit supplied by the vehicle when the car supports it.
  • Map Data uses downloaded map information for the current road.
  • Vision uses the road camera to detect speed-limit signs.

Use Primary Speed Limit Source to select the first source SLC should trust. Use Secondary Speed Limit Source to select a backup when the primary source is unavailable. Highest and Lowest can be selected as the primary behavior when you want SLC to choose between available limits by value.

Use Mapbox as Fallback allows Mapbox data to provide a limit when the configured sources do not have one.

Vision speed limits

Vision Speed Limit Detection is experimental and can misread signs. Use confirmation for new limits and keep another source available until vision detection is reliable in your area.

docs.title: Vision speed limits
docs.text:
In Galaxy, open Toggles → Longitudinal (Speed & Following) → Speed Limit Controller. Set Primary source or Secondary source to Vision, with dashboard or maps as another available source. If Vision is absent from the source choices, camera sign detection is unavailable on this device or build. Show speed limit signs only changes the display; turn on Speed Limit Controller if you want accepted limits to affect cruise speed.

Check camera-reported limits against road signs. Automatic adoption applies a new limit after a brief flash; turn it off to require confirmation. Start with conservative offsets while evaluating Vision. To help improve detection, follow the route submission steps.

docs.title: Configure speed offsets
docs.text:
SLC supports a separate offset for each posted-speed range:

Posted speed Setting 0 to 24 mph Speed Offset (0-24 mph) 25 to 34 mph Speed Offset (25-34 mph) 35 to 44 mph Speed Offset (35-44 mph) 45 to 54 mph Speed Offset (45-54 mph) 55 to 64 mph Speed Offset (55-64 mph) 65 to 74 mph Speed Offset (65-74 mph) 75 to 99 mph Speed Offset (75-99 mph)

A positive offset allows a target above the posted limit. A negative offset sets the target below it. For example, a 55 mph limit with a +5 mph offset produces an SLC target of 60 mph.

Enable Show Speed Limit Offset to display the active offset on the driving screen.

docs.title: Confirm new speed limits
docs.text:
Enable Confirm New Speed Limits if you want SLC to ask before applying a changed limit. You can require confirmation separately for higher and lower limits.

When confirmation is requested:

  • Tap the flashing speed-limit widget or press Cruise Increase to accept the new limit.
  • Press Cruise Decrease to deny it.
  • Ignoring the prompt for 30 seconds also denies it.

Confirmation is useful when map or vision data sometimes reports incorrect limits.

docs.title: Look ahead for changes
docs.text:
Higher Limit Lookahead Time and Lower Limit Lookahead Time control how far ahead SLC anticipates upcoming map-based speed-limit changes. Each setting can be configured from 0 to 30 seconds.

A lower-limit lookahead gives the vehicle time to slow before entering a reduced-speed area. A higher-limit lookahead determines how early SLC can prepare for an upcoming increase.

docs.title: Match the limit when engaging
docs.text:
Enable Match Speed Limit on Engage to set the maximum driving speed to the current posted limit when openpilot first engages.

If this is disabled, the driver's existing maximum set speed remains in effect until SLC needs to limit it.

docs.title: Choose fallback behavior
docs.text:
Fallback Speed controls what happens when no speed-limit source is available:

  • Set Speed uses the driver's current maximum set speed.
  • Experimental Mode allows the driving model to manage speed while no limit is available.
  • Previous Limit continues using the most recent valid speed limit.

Choose the fallback that best matches how you want StarPilot to behave when map, dashboard, and vision data are unavailable.

docs.title: Override SLC
docs.text:
Override Speed controls what happens when you manually drive faster than the SLC target:

  • None does not create an SLC override.
  • Set With Gas Pedal uses the speed reached with the accelerator as the override.
  • Max Set Speed allows the driver's maximum set speed to override SLC.

An override does not change the posted speed limit. It only changes the speed SLC allows until the override ends or conditions change.

docs.title: Show source information
docs.text:
Enable Show Speed Limit Sources to display each available source and its current value on the driving screen.

Additional display options can:

  • Show abbreviated source names.
  • Hide sources that do not currently have a speed limit.
  • Show the active speed-limit offset.

These options are useful when checking why SLC selected a particular limit.

docs.title: Incorrect or missing map limits
docs.text:
Map-based speed limits come from OpenStreetMap. If a road has an incorrect or missing limit, correct it in OpenStreetMap. The updated map data may take about a week to reach the device.

See Vision Speed Limit Detection if you want to help improve camera-based sign detection.

Start conservatively

Start with confirmation enabled and small offsets. Display the source information while testing so you can see where each limit came from. Change one setting at a time and verify its behavior before relying on it regularly.

docs.title: StarPort
docs.text: Open Galaxy → Tools → StarPort while parked. Choose your device, follow its setup steps, then connect. Supported setups include built-in Android Auto, AAWireless and Motorola MA1 wireless adapters, and the Open Headunit and HeadunitPad tablet apps. Other adapters and apps may work but are not tested and may be unreliable.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
1. Under StarPort Support, turn on StarPort and choose Install support. Download a current stable Android Auto package by Google LLC and upload it without unzipping it. Wait for support to show Ready. Wireless pairing needs Bluetooth; accept Galaxy's prompt to enable it if needed.
  2. Choose your connection and follow the matching instructions:
    • Built-in wireless: Open the car's phone pairing screen, tap Find car, select the car, and confirm the pairing code on both screens. Enable wireless Android Auto in the car's settings if needed; it may be called smartphone connection or phone projection.
    • Wireless adapter: Choose the adapter, put it in pairing mode, and tap Find adapter. Select the adapter as the receiver. If Galaxy asks you to connect your paired car in Bluetooth first, open Galaxy → Tools → Bluetooth, connect the car, and return to StarPort.
    • USB cable: Connect the car's Android Auto USB data port to the comma with a data-capable cable, then tap Connect. Bluetooth pairing is not needed. In the expanded setup, this option is called Wired AA.
    • Tablet app: Choose the app, open it on the tablet on the same Wi-Fi network as the comma, then tap Connect.
  3. Tap Connect and keep the car on and its screen awake. The first connection can take a few minutes and sometimes more than one drive while StarPort finds a working setup. Later connections use what worked before.

Enable Automatic Connection to connect when you start driving. Use Setup and Pairing or Change how your car connects to reopen setup.

docs.title: Connection problems
docs.text:
Check that StarPort support shows Ready, the correct car or adapter is selected, and Bluetooth and wireless Android Auto are enabled when using a wireless receiver. Other paired phones may take the screen first.

Status What to check Connecting over Bluetooth or Finding Android Auto Keep the car on and the selected receiver paired. Starting wireless setup or Waiting for car Wi-Fi Enable wireless Android Auto and check whether another phone is using it. Getting car Wi-Fi details or Joining car Wi-Fi Follow the displayed instructions; restart the car or adapter if this repeatedly fails. Securing your connection Check the support certificate and update or reinstall support if needed. Waiting for your USB cable Use the car's Android Auto data port and a data-capable cable. Connected · car screen in use Open Android Auto on the car screen to return to StarPilot. Trying your connection again Allow the automatic reconnect and follow any displayed instructions. Your dashboard is live StarPilot is showing on the screen.

For a black or frozen screen, tap Disconnect, wait a few seconds, and connect again. If it keeps happening, turn the car off, wait for its screen to go dark, and restart it. If a wireless adapter hangs repeatedly, unplug it for ten seconds and plug it back in. StarPort continues automatically or offers Continue.

Use Connection Logs on the StarPort page when asking for help. The logs page includes the last 20 sessions.

docs.title: Other phones and audio
docs.text:
Most cars run Android Auto on one device at a time. If another phone keeps taking over, choose the comma as the preferred device where supported, disable that phone's wireless Android Auto for this car, or remove unused pairings.

Open StarPort → Spotify and Phone Audio for music and phone audio. For phone audio, pair your phone through Bluetooth first.

docs.title: Layout, maps, and upkeep
docs.text:
• Customize Layout opens the StarPort layout editor.
  • Offline Road Maps saves road lines for the map overlay. For destinations and other map downloads, see Navigation & Maps.
  • Wireless projection may use the comma's Wi-Fi for the car instead of its usual network. Use the Galaxy hotspot for local access; remote Galaxy needs an Internet connection on the comma.
  • If the support certificate expires soon or has expired, open StarPort Support and use Update or Reinstall as offered.

docs.title: Start over
docs.text: Forget the receiver in Galaxy's Bluetooth page and remove the comma from the receiver's paired-device list. Restart the car or adapter, reopen its pairing screen, then follow the matching StarPort setup again.

docs.title: Chestnut (External GPU)
docs.text:
Chestnut is comma.ai's external GPU (eGPU) dock. It connects a desktop graphics card to your comma device over USB4, giving openpilot far more compute than the built-in chip can provide on its own.

StarPilot fully supports Chestnut on the Comma 3, Comma 3X, and Comma 4.

Learn more from comma.ai: Introducing chestnut · Chestnut shop

docs.title: What does Chestnut do?
docs.text:
Comma devices are built around low-power, on-device inference — roughly a 10 W compute budget. That works well for most driving models, but newer chestnut-class models are much larger and need a desktop GPU to run in real time.

Chestnut bridges that gap. You mount a GPU in the passenger footwell or under the passenger seat, connect it to 12 V power, and plug a USB cable into your comma device. At startup, model weights load over USB4; after that, inference runs entirely on the GPU.

docs.title: Do I need Chestnut?
docs.text:
Most StarPilot driving models run on the comma device's built-in compute. Chestnut lets you run supported Big models locally and is required for Model pair. Jetlink is another option for running a single Big model on a remote host; see Models.

On Galaxy’s Models page:

  • Models that need external hardware are labeled accordingly on the Models page.
  • You can download a Big model before connecting Chestnut. It runs only when compatible GPU hardware is ready.
  • Without an external GPU or an active Jetlink host, StarPilot uses Active Small. Your Big selection remains saved.

StarPilot checks for Chestnut at boot.

docs.title: Hardware options
docs.text: Comma sells tiny chestnut, a dock that needs your own GPU and power supply, and Ready to drive, a kit with GPU and power hardware. See comma's shop for current options.

docs.title: Setup overview
docs.text:
This is a high-level summary. Follow comma's included instructions (or their blog) for the full install:

  1. Assemble Chestnut with your GPU and connect GPU power.
  2. Mount Chestnut in the passenger footwell or under the passenger seat.
  3. Connect Chestnut to 12 V vehicle power (cigarette lighter or similar).
  4. Run the USB cable from Chestnut to your comma device's USB4 port.
  5. Boot StarPilot — the device should detect Chestnut automatically.

Firmware

Chestnut ships with custom firmware that StarPilot recognizes. The device checks that the firmware is ready before enabling GPU models. If GPU models stay unavailable after connecting Chestnut, ask in Discord.

Driving models

See Models for the current catalog. Most users should start with an on-device model.

docs.title: Comma Pedal
docs.text:
The Comma Pedal is an interceptor that sits between your throttle pedal and the car. When openpilot is disengaged, your throttle pedal is normal. When openpilot is engaged, openpilot can send its own throttle pedal commands to control your speed, but will immediately stop sending its own commands when you override or disengage.

For non-ACC vehicles (flashed ACC also excluded), the comma pedal will be used to accelerate and "brake" using regen in one-pedal mode. For ACC vehicles, the ACC commands will be used to control gas/brake, but the Comma Pedal will be used to exit standstill (slight tap of the throttle to start moving).

You always have control, so you can input your own throttle commands at any time, overriding openpilot control if it is engaged. Openpilot will also disengage in the same way as stock CC: when you press the brake pedal, throttle pedal, regen paddle, CC cancel button, or CC off button.

docs.title: Pedal Purchase List
docs.text:
Important

This hardware is only necessary if indicated by your car setup guide

  • Comma Pedal
  • Ethernet cable
    • At least 10ft long (reaches from harness box to throttle pedal)
    • Cat5e is sufficient (higher ratings will be thicker and harder to route under the car's headliner)
    • Flat cables can be easier to route, but quality can be more variable than round cables.
  • Optional: DFU Key
    • If the firmware is ever updated, you need a DFU key (or DIY if you are mechanically inclined) to apply new firmware. See the Bolt pedal firmware instructions for details.

Bundle your pedal with a harness box.

If you already have a Harness Cable, but your Harness Box does not have an RJ45 port (or you do not have one), you can bundle your Pedal with a 2x9 or 2x13 pin Harness Box - check your specific cable to ensure you purchase the correct box.

docs.title: Comma Devices
docs.text:
StarPilot supports the Comma 3, Comma 3X, and Comma 4. All three devices provide the cameras, processing, driver monitoring, storage, and vehicle connection needed to run StarPilot. The correct choice mostly depends on what you already own, whether your car uses CAN FD, and whether you want to buy new or used hardware.

Check your car first

A comma device does not connect directly to every car. Check the StarPilot car support page and the comma supported vehicles list before buying anything. Your vehicle may require a specific harness, connector, pedal, or other hardware.

The device does not determine how much steering torque, braking control, or acceleration control your car has. Those capabilities depend on the vehicle and its installed hardware.

docs.title: Comma 4
docs.text:
The Comma 4 is comma.ai's current device and is the recommended option for most people buying new hardware. It uses a Snapdragon 845 MAX, includes 128 GB of storage, supports CAN FD without an additional panda, and has LTE, Wi-Fi, GPS, night-vision driver monitoring, and three cameras.

The Comma 4 provides the same general compute, sensor suite, and functionality as the Comma 3X in a body that comma.ai describes as one-fifth the size. Its cooling system is designed for sustained performance, and its small OLED display is used for status and driving information instead of the large touchscreen found on the Comma 3 and 3X.

Purchase from comma.ai: Comma 4

Mounts

Comma 4 mounts are different from Comma 3 and 3X mounts. If you replace an older device with a Comma 4, install the mount supplied for the Comma 4.

docs.title: Comma 3X
docs.text:
The Comma 3X uses a Snapdragon 845, three 1080p HDR cameras, a 2160 x 1080 OLED touchscreen, 128 GB of storage, LTE, Wi-Fi, GPS, and infrared lighting for driver monitoring. CAN FD support is built in, so it does not require a separate red panda for CAN FD vehicles.

Comma.ai introduced the Comma 3X as a less complex replacement for the Comma 3 with the same general performance and triple-camera system. It remains a good StarPilot device if you already own one or find a used unit in good condition.

Comma.ai now sells the Comma 4 as its current device. Comma 3X units are generally found through the used market or the comma.ai community Discord.

docs.title: Comma 3
docs.text:
The Comma 3 is the oldest of the three devices supported by StarPilot. It uses the same Snapdragon 845 family and triple-camera layout as the Comma 3X, so existing owners can still run current StarPilot releases.

Comma.ai ended official Comma 3 software support on August 26, 2025 to focus on newer hardware. Stock openpilot no longer supports it. StarPilot and some other forks continue to support the Comma 3, but buying one is not advised. Existing owners can continue using it with a supporting fork.

CAN FD vehicles

A Comma 3 requires a red panda to communicate with a CAN FD vehicle. The Comma 3X and Comma 4 have CAN FD support built in. Existing Comma 3 owners should check their vehicle before purchasing a replacement panda.

docs.title: What else do I need?
docs.text:
A typical installation requires:

  • A supported comma device
  • The correct car harness and harness connector
  • A harness box
  • An OBD-C cable
  • A compatible windshield mount

Some StarPilot-supported vehicles need additional hardware, such as a pedal, GM harness, ASCM or SDGM integration, or an OBD-C setup that differs from comma's stock installation. Follow the guide for your specific vehicle rather than ordering from the general list alone.

See the following pages before installation:

  • Car support
  • Installing your Comma device
  • Installing StarPilot
  • OBD-C cable
  • Comma Pedal

docs.title: Buying a used device
docs.text:
Before buying a used Comma 3X, confirm that:

  1. The device boots and reaches its setup screen.
  2. The road and driver-monitoring cameras work and are unobstructed.
  3. The display, USB-C port, Wi-Fi, and GPS work correctly.
  4. The listing includes the correct mount and cable, or you have replacements available.
  5. You know whether your vehicle requires CAN FD.
  6. You can obtain the correct harness and any StarPilot-specific hardware for your car.

Do not assume that a used device includes the correct harness for your vehicle or qualifies for comma.ai warranty service or trade-in credit. The Comma 3 is end-of-life hardware, so buying one is not advised even though StarPilot and some other community forks continue to support it.

docs.title: Optional hardware and services
docs.text:
StarPilot can pair a comma device with Galaxy for remote settings and device management. Comma Prime is optional and is not required to run StarPilot.

StarPilot also supports Chestnut for users who want to run larger driving models with an external GPU. Most users do not need Chestnut.

docs.title: Which one should I choose?
docs.text:
• Buy a Comma 4 if you want new hardware, built-in CAN FD support, and the smallest current device.
  • Keep using a Comma 3X if you already have one. There is no need to replace a working device solely to run StarPilot.
  • Buying a Comma 3 is not advised. You can keep using one if you already own it and plan to remain on StarPilot or another fork that supports it.

Regardless of the device, you must remain attentive and ready to take control. StarPilot and openpilot are driver-assistance systems, not self-driving systems.
